To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
local immune activation may modulates HIV-1 shedding with possible influence on the vaginal physiology and host defense.

(1) local immune activation in the genital mucosa is a key factor in the modulation of HIV-1 shedding; (2) local immune activation may have an influence on vaginal physiology; (3) the local immune response is modulated by HIV-1 replication and antiretrovial drugs; (4) the cytokine pattern in cervico-vagina secretions is less favourable to the spread of HIV infection among antiretrovially treated women.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the immune system and its response to infection, in order to better understand the mechanisms that underlie the pathogenesis of HIV infection and to develop new therapeutic strategies.
the identification of the factors associated with HIV shedding and with the development of a new model of local immunopathogenesis of HIV disease in women.
the identification of factors that may influence HIV-1 shedding and vaginal immunity in order to better target prevention strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
local immune activation may modulated HIV-1 shedding, and that pharmacological agents lowering HIV replication cause a shift in cytokine production which is less favourable to transmission of HIV-1.
the presence of HIV-1 in the cervico-vagina may be related with local proinflammatory responses and the presence of SIL.
the presence of local immune activation may modulates HIV-1 shedding with possible influence on local vaginal physiology and host defense.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV infected women who have high levels of cytokines in the vagina have higher levels of HIV in the cervico-vagina.
local immunity may be an important determinant in the transmission of HIV-1 infection.
the presence of local pro-inflammatory cytokines in cervico-vagina is a marker of HIV-1 related nucleic acids and is associated with factors known to influence vaginal physiology and host defense.
The main takeaway from our work is that
local immune responses in the female reproductive tract are modulated by HIV infection and that the local cytokine environment may play a role in HIV transmission.
the presence of HIV RNA in cervico vaginal secretions, and the presence of local pro-inflammatory cytokines are associated with the presence of SIL.
local immune activation may modulates HIV-1 shedding.
